name: MegaTTS3
description: ByteDance's lightweight diffusion-transformer zero-shot TTS engine with voice cloning and bilingual (Chinese/English) synthesis. Self-hosted via a Gradio web UI (tts/gradio_api.py, default port 7860). Ships a first-party Dockerfile. The README documents a remote-exposure launch recipe with placeholder credentials, making misconfigured public instances a likely find.
auth_notes: No authentication by default. The Gradio UI (tts/gradio_api.py) binds 127.0.0.1:7860 with no auth. Notably the README documents a remote launch recipe: 'GRADIO_SERVER_NAME=0.0.0.0 GRADIO_USERNAME=admin GRADIO_PASSWORD=change_me python tts/gradio_api.py' - operators who copy this to expose the UI but drop the USERNAME/PASSWORD env vars get an unauthenticated 0.0.0.0-bound instance, and those who keep the doc'd placeholder ship the weak default credential admin:change_me. Both the missing-cred and placeholder-cred cases are active hunting signals. No token, no rate limiting by default.

shodan_dorks.rationale: MegaTTS3 serves a Gradio SPA; the static HTML shell contains the gradio-app mount and asset references but not the project name. Catches the Gradio surface on the canonical port for follow-up confirmation.

Name match reachable only when the Gradio version inlines window.gradio_config (the gr.Markdown banner) into the served HTML; Shodan-blind on versions that lazy-fetch /config. High-precision where config is inlined.

Conjunctive: Gradio mount plus the inlined MegaTTS3 banner isolates it from other Gradio TTS apps; otherwise resolve via /config fetch or aimap deep-enum. Instances behind the doc'd basic-auth recipe return a 401 challenge on the Gradio surface - a secondary discriminator.
MegaTTS3 model identifier in the inlined config banner distinguishes this release; use for version-targeted enumeration on config-inlined deployments.

known_vulns: No built-in auth on the Gradio UI by default - unauthenticated voice cloning when bound to 0.0.0.0
Documented weak default credential admin:change_me from the README remote-launch recipe (basic auth), plus the unauth case when operators omit the USERNAME/PASSWORD env vars
Gradio CVE-2024-1561 - arbitrary local file read via component routes on unpatched pins
Gradio CVE-2023-51449 - path traversal via /file= on Gradio 3.x < 3.47.0
Gradio CVE-2024-1727 - CSRF chain against /file and upload routes on Gradio 4.x pre-patch
SSRF via /queue/join upload proxy in the 2024 Gradio 4.x security batch
Unauthenticated GPU compute consumption - no rate limiting on inference by default
share=True tunnel exposure - public *.gradio.live URL bypasses local network controls
risk_notes: MegaTTS3 is the standout exposure risk of the ByteDance/Gradio TTS cohort because the README publishes the exact 0.0.0.0-bind launch command and ships a first-party Docker image, so misconfigured public instances are the most likely to appear. Primary vectors: (1) Zero-shot voice cloning without auth - attacker uploads a reference clip and synthesizes arbitrary bilingual speech in that voice (deepfake/vishing); (2) Weak/placeholder credential admin:change_me - operators who follow the doc verbatim ship a guessable basic-auth pair; those who drop the env vars ship no auth at all; (3) GPU compute theft on the ungated inference queue; (4) File-read/traversal on instances pinned to a vulnerable Gradio version (CVE-2024-1561 / CVE-2023-51449) via /file=; (5) reference-audio PII stored server-side. Shodan http.html is largely blind to the MegaTTS name (JS SPA; title 'Gradio', mount div id='gradio-app'); identity lives in /config JSON. Instances behind the doc'd basic auth answer the Gradio surface with a 401 - a useful secondary discriminator when hunting the recipe's followers.
deployment_notes: Released 2025-03-22 by ByteDance. Default deployment is 'python tts/gradio_api.py' binding 127.0.0.1:7860 (docs: 'Visit http://127.0.0.1:7860/ for gradio'). A first-party Dockerfile builds image tag megatts3:latest ('Docker version currently under testing'); the local run maps -p 127.0.0.1:7860:7860, while the documented remote variant maps -p 7860:7860 on all interfaces. Exposure occurs via the README's GRADIO_SERVER_NAME=0.0.0.0 recipe. Server header is 'uvicorn'. Shodan indexes only the SPA shell, so pivot on the /config endpoint, gradio-app mount, title 'Gradio', the uvicorn header, and the 401 basic-auth challenge for recipe-followers; Censys with a config fetch or aimap deep-enum resolves the true identity. The full model weights (WaveVAE encoder) are gated by ByteDance, so many public instances run inference-only with the released decoder.
